name: Getscreen
summary: Browser-based remote desktop and remote-support software: connect to any computer with no client install, share one-click access links, transfer files and record sessions. Built for IT teams, MSPs and remote support.
best_for: IT and support people who want to connect from a browser and can ask the other person to run a small file: at a fair price or a one-time fee
skip_if: you need the absolute lowest latency (AnyDesk) or heavy compliance certifications like HIPAA/SOC 2 (TeamViewer)
honest_knock: AnyDesk tends to feel faster and lower-latency, and TeamViewer carries the heavier security/compliance certifications (HIPAA, SOC 2). Getscreen's real edge is that you connect from a browser and that it is cheaper, especially with the lifetime deal; for a one-off session the other person still has to download and run a file.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-09-23) Business rates on getscreen.me/en/pricing/plans/ are quoted on annual payment, which the page marks 16% off. The figures were first read over a US connection on 2026-08-26 as dollars and have not moved since; from a Dutch connection the same numerals print as euros, so the currency symbol follows the visitor region rather than the price. The business subscription bills on two meters at once, and quoting only the first understates it: Standard is $4.17 per technician a month plus $0.08 per device, Advanced $6.67 plus $0.13, and Enterprise $8.33 plus $0.17. Advanced and Enterprise add unlimited client invitations. Free plan (2 devices); paid tiers add one-time quick connections (Advanced) and white-label, roles and mass-device management (Enterprise) — plus a one-time Personal Lifetime Deal at $149 in the page as served, which a browser on a European connection re-renders as EUR 139 (a different number, not just a different symbol, unlike the business rates), and which sidesteps the recurring fees of rivals like TeamViewer (~$50/mo). Without annual payment the business rates are 5.00 / 8.00 / 10.00 per technician and 0.10 / 0.15 / 0.20 per device a month (Standard / Advanced / Enterprise). The HTTP API is absent on Standard and limited to 100 requests per hour per device on Advanced and 1,000 on Enterprise; video recording storage is 1 GB, 2 GB and 5 GB per technician.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Getscreen in the 14-day trial of an account we created. The trial needed no card and showed limits of 500 devices and 5 technicians. A Quick Support invitation was ready in under a minute. Its client page, however, asks the client to download and run a file and offered no way to join from the browser, so no session was connected. The purchase window showed Advanced at EUR 7.9 a month on yearly billing and EUR 9.5 a month on monthly billing; Buy Now was not clicked. Account and start: we created the account; our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab on getscreen.me/panel, on 19 November 2026 from 09:33 CET. The interface was already in English. Nothing was installed, downloaded or sent. The dossier name is Getscreen and the review is on AIBM (b2b/getscreen-review). The account opened with Your trial subscription is activated: access to the trial plan with all options and limits for 500 devices and 5 technicians, 14 days left. Rate Plan showed Service plan Trial, expiration date 03.12.2026, 500 devices (0% used), 5 technicians (1 of 5 used), Unlimited invitations, 25 GB video recording and 500000 HTTP API requests per hour. No card was asked for the account or the trial. The free plan of 2 devices was not shown in the app during the trial. Core action, a one-off support invitation: Quick Support, Create an Invitation made an invitation at 09:34:18, in under a minute and two clicks. The window Invite a Client says that when a client runs the attached file from the invite, you will be able to control their desktop, and offers an e-mail, a link or a code. The client page behind the link was opened but nothing on it was clicked: it says the session is a trial version not intended for serving real clients, asks the client to download and run the attached file, and lists files for Windows, macOS and Linux. That page offered no way to join in the browser without the file, so no screen was shared and no session was connected. Team, Technicians was empty; Role Management lists the system roles for devices, invitations and administration. Settings has Team, Branding, Integrations, Gateways, API Keys and Self-Hosted; branding was not set and was not turned on. Plans: On getscreen.me/en/pricing/plans/, billed yearly with 16% off and shown in EUR from a Dutch connection: Standard 4.17 per technician plus 0.08 per device a month, Advanced 6.67 plus 0.13 and Enterprise 8.33 plus 0.17; Quick Support has unlimited invitations on Advanced and Enterprise and is not in Standard; the HTTP API is absent on Standard, 100 requests per hour per device on Advanced and 1000 on Enterprise. In the app Buy a Subscription, with Advanced preselected for 10 devices and 1 technician, shows Monthly Subscription EUR 9.5 a month and Annual Subscription EUR 7.9 a month (16% cheaper). The window also shows Trial Subscription Free, 14 days, Not available for this plan, and the payment marks Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Alipay. Checkout: Buy Now was not clicked, so no payment page, card field, tax or total was seen. Cancelling: no cancel button for the trial was seen; the trial ends on 03.12.2026 and no subscription is attached. Account, Profile has a bin icon to delete the account, which was not clicked. Cancelling a paid plan was not tested. Not tested: the agent on a device, screen sharing in the browser, a connected session, inviting a technician, branding, device groups, the API, the free plan after the trial and the lifetime deal. Clean up: the account and the trial stay; one test invitation stays open in Quick Support, never sent, and expires by itself. The own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The client side of a Quick Support invitation asks for a downloaded file, and the trial client page warns the client not to trust the technician with their computer, so a trial is hard to use with a real customer. The purchase window marks the 14-day trial as not available for the chosen plan while the account is already in a trial.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Getscreen in the 14-day trial of an account we created. The trial needed no card and showed limits of 500 devices and 5 technicians. A Quick Support invitation was ready in under a minute. Its client page, however, asks the client to download and run a file and offered no way to join from the browser, so no session was connected. The purchase window showed Advanced at EUR 7.9 a month on yearly billing and EUR 9.5 a month on monthly billing; Buy Now was not clicked. Account and start: we created the account; our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab on getscreen.me/panel, on 19 November 2026 from 09:33 CET. The interface was already in English. Nothing was installed, downloaded or sent. The dossier name is Getscreen and the review is on AIBM (b2b/getscreen-review). The account opened with Your trial subscription is activated: access to the trial plan with all options and limits for 500 devices and 5 technicians, 14 days left. Rate Plan showed Service plan Trial, expiration date 03.12.2026, 500 devices (0% used), 5 technicians (1 of 5 used), Unlimited invitations, 25 GB video recording and 500000 HTTP API requests per hour. No card was asked for the account or the trial. The free plan of 2 devices was not shown in the app during the trial. Core action, a one-off support invitation: Quick Support, Create an Invitation made an invitation at 09:34:18, in under a minute and two clicks. The window Invite a Client says that when a client runs the attached file from the invite, you will be able to control their desktop, and offers an e-mail, a link or a code. The client page behind the link was opened but nothing on it was clicked: it says the session is a trial version not intended for serving real clients, asks the client to download and run the attached file, and lists files for Windows, macOS and Linux. That page offered no way to join in the browser without the file, so no screen was shared and no session was connected. Team, Technicians was empty; Role Management lists the system roles for devices, invitations and administration. Settings has Team, Branding, Integrations, Gateways, API Keys and Self-Hosted; branding was not set and was not turned on. Plans: On getscreen.me/en/pricing/plans/, billed yearly with 16% off and shown in EUR from a Dutch connection: Standard 4.17 per technician plus 0.08 per device a month, Advanced 6.67 plus 0.13 and Enterprise 8.33 plus 0.17; Quick Support has unlimited invitations on Advanced and Enterprise and is not in Standard; the HTTP API is absent on Standard, 100 requests per hour per device on Advanced and 1000 on Enterprise. In the app Buy a Subscription, with Advanced preselected for 10 devices and 1 technician, shows Monthly Subscription EUR 9.5 a month and Annual Subscription EUR 7.9 a month (16% cheaper). The window also shows Trial Subscription Free, 14 days, Not available for this plan, and the payment marks Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Alipay. Checkout: Buy Now was not clicked, so no payment page, card field, tax or total was seen. Cancelling: no cancel button for the trial was seen; the trial ends on 03.12.2026 and no subscription is attached. Account, Profile has a bin icon to delete the account, which was not clicked. Cancelling a paid plan was not tested. Not tested: the agent on a device, screen sharing in the browser, a connected session, inviting a technician, branding, device groups, the API, the free plan after the trial and the lifetime deal. Clean up: the account and the trial stay; one test invitation stays open in Quick Support, never sent, and expires by itself. The own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The client side of a Quick Support invitation asks for a downloaded file, and the trial client page warns the client not to trust the technician with their computer, so a trial is hard to use with a real customer. The purchase window marks the 14-day trial as not available for the chosen plan while the account is already in a trial.
